UNSC Reborn v0.6.3 - "It Was Locked for a Reason""  
Download

Requires

Lazylib

and

MagicLib

. Nexerelin supported.

A rebuild of

AppleMarineXX's

UNSC mod, picked up after three years - the faction, the lore and most of the art are theirs. I wanted the ships to be the size they are in the books, and then I could not stop.

The Infinity is 5,694 metres long. She is now 5,694 metres long.

Lore (Subject to change):

The gate did not only move the colony fleet. When it fired, it took a bite of Epsilon Eridani with it - a volume of space roughly where Reach used to be, and everything still in orbit. That included the graveyard. It also took whatever else happened to be in that volume, which in 2552 was a Covenant battlegroup in the middle of glassing the place. They came through intact. They have no idea where they are, no route home, and no interest in either question - the fleet that burned Reach is simply carrying on with it here. Somewhere behind the anchorage at Reverence, a San'Shyuum is explaining that this is all part of the plan.

Features:

The UNSC: 34 warships, 2 civilian hulls, 7 strike craft and 3 tiers of Anchor station, every one sized from its canonical length - an 82m Winter prowler against a 1,192m Marathon, and the Infinity above everything.The Covenant: 24 warships from the DAV corvette to the CAS assault carrier, a tithe freighter, 5 strike craft, 2 tiers of anchorage, and 4 fixed installations that are there to be looked at rather than fought.Every warship armed from its canonical armament table, not from a balance guideline - the Marathon is 83% missile pods where Halopedia says 84%, the Strident 11% where canon says 11%. Carriers launch a real air group: twenty-two aircraft off an Infinity.22 UNSC weapons - the MAC line, Archer pods, Shiva nukes, Rampart point defence. 12 Covenant weapons - energy projectors, plasma torpedoes, pulse lasers in three weights, needlers, fuel rods. No vanilla blueprints in either faction.Two ways to survive being shot at. The Covenant hold Energy Projection Screens - cheap to run, quick to re-form, with very little ship behind them. The UNSC holds armour, and that is the entire list.The Covenant Hierarchy - seven grades from Minor to Imperial Admiral, earned in devotion for fighting the Covenant's war and lost slowly when you do not. A Council of six named San'Shyuum and Sangheili, each with their own reading of what you are for.The Luminary Array - carry one and Forerunner relics start turning up in ordinary salvage, so every wreck and ruin already scattered across the sector becomes worth sweeping. They cannot be sold to anybody. They buy standing, and the vault is counting.The tithe - hand your holds to the Ministry for credits and devotion, which is the Covenant's answer to the trade fleet they will not let you run.ONI's three Sections - intelligence, influence and clearance, earned separately and spent on different things. Clearance answers to deniable work actually completed, not to your rank, so buying grades no longer quietly buys the secrets.Standing orders - Section Three describes how the war is actually going and tells you what to do about it, calibrated against a live measure of how much of the sector's economy the Covenant holds.A fleet operations board - eleven kinds of line work from derelict sweeps to counter-intelligence, opening by service grade rather than clearance, posted against UNSC space and paid in intelligence and influence.Prize crews - win a boarding action with marines aboard and keep the hull, at a price in marines that scales with what you are trying to take.Three desks that do not like each other - Sections One and Two have catalogues of their own now, and buying from one costs you standing with the other two. A desk that owes you charges less; a desk you have ignored for a year charges more, and far enough into the red it declines its best work.Captured technology - Covenant hardware comes off the wrecks you make of them, and three permanent programmes turn it into things the UNSC could never build. The hullmods have no other source: no shop, no cache, no blueprint.A front line that moves - the Covenant gather a suppression force, sail it across the sector under its own power, and burn a world if nobody stops them. Intercept it in transit, break it in orbit, or lose the planet - and killing it costs them months, not a reset.The Great Schism - serve them long enough, and carry enough relics to the vault, and a Sangheili shipmaster asks what you intend to do with what the Oracle actually said. It is the only way out of the Covenant the mod has ever had.Epsilon Eridani, with a graveyard holding the Pillar of Autumn, Iroquois, Gettysburg, In Amber Clad and Forward Unto Dawn - and the Spirit of Fire still drifting, alone, further out. Every one of them still has its flight recorder aboard.Reverence - the stranded battlegroup's anchorage, built around a forge world and covered by its own stations. It is the only Covenant port in the sector, and they are not taking visitors.ONI Section Three on every UNSC world, dealing in fleet stores, ODST detachments, archive access and work nobody writes down.Black operations - six deniable contracts against UNSC hardware in the wrong hands, plus a job board running courier work, dead drops, prisoner transfers, infiltration, extraction and sabotage on the ground with Marines instead of guns. Paid in credits and requisition chits.Requisition and standing - chits buy your way up the twelve-grade UNSC ladder from Warrant Officer to Fleet Admiral, raising your stipend and unlocking what the ONI desk will hand over.Undercover cells in the capital of every other faction in the sector. You will not find one on a menu - at Lieutenant Commander, someone starts waiting for you in the bar, and only after that drink does the door open. They deal in stolen local stores, rewritten records, and whatever nine months of deep cover has quietly put aside.Four custom industries, each taking a colony item only the UNSC makes.Twelve ship systems, six hullmods including a fleet-wide Shipboard AI, and eleven combat missions - two of which put you on the Covenant side of the fight.Custom portraits for both factions, finally, after three versions of borrowed vanilla faces - and the picture picks the name. Choose a UNSC portrait at character creation, and you get a UNSC name; choose a Covenant one, and you very much do not. Their officers and fleet commanders are named the same way.

Compatibility:

not save-compatible with the original UNSC mod, and not meant to be run alongside it - both define the same faction and the same ship IDs.

descriptionHtml:
UNSC Reborn v0.6.3 - "It Was Locked for a Reason"" 
Download
Requires Lazylib and MagicLib. Nexerelin supported.
A rebuild of AppleMarineXX's UNSC mod, picked up after three years - the faction, the lore and most of the art are theirs. I wanted the ships to be the size they are in the books, and then I could not stop.
The Infinity is 5,694 metres long. She is now 5,694 metres long.
Lore (Subject to change): The gate did not only move the colony fleet. When it fired, it took a bite of Epsilon Eridani with it - a volume of space roughly where Reach used to be, and everything still in orbit. That included the graveyard. It also took whatever else happened to be in that volume, which in 2552 was a Covenant battlegroup in the middle of glassing the place. They came through intact. They have no idea where they are, no route home, and no interest in either question - the fleet that burned Reach is simply carrying on with it here. Somewhere behind the anchorage at Reverence, a San'Shyuum is explaining that this is all part of the plan.

Features:
  • The UNSC: 34 warships, 2 civilian hulls, 7 strike craft and 3 tiers of Anchor station, every one sized from its canonical length - an 82m Winter prowler against a 1,192m Marathon, and the Infinity above everything.
  • The Covenant: 24 warships from the DAV corvette to the CAS assault carrier, a tithe freighter, 5 strike craft, 2 tiers of anchorage, and 4 fixed installations that are there to be looked at rather than fought.
  • Every warship armed from its canonical armament table, not from a balance guideline - the Marathon is 83% missile pods where Halopedia says 84%, the Strident 11% where canon says 11%. Carriers launch a real air group: twenty-two aircraft off an Infinity.
  • 22 UNSC weapons - the MAC line, Archer pods, Shiva nukes, Rampart point defence. 12 Covenant weapons - energy projectors, plasma torpedoes, pulse lasers in three weights, needlers, fuel rods. No vanilla blueprints in either faction.
  • Two ways to survive being shot at. The Covenant hold Energy Projection Screens - cheap to run, quick to re-form, with very little ship behind them. The UNSC holds armour, and that is the entire list.
  • The Covenant Hierarchy - seven grades from Minor to Imperial Admiral, earned in devotion for fighting the Covenant's war and lost slowly when you do not. A Council of six named San'Shyuum and Sangheili, each with their own reading of what you are for.
  • The Luminary Array - carry one and Forerunner relics start turning up in ordinary salvage, so every wreck and ruin already scattered across the sector becomes worth sweeping. They cannot be sold to anybody. They buy standing, and the vault is counting.
  • The tithe - hand your holds to the Ministry for credits and devotion, which is the Covenant's answer to the trade fleet they will not let you run.
  • ONI's three Sections - intelligence, influence and clearance, earned separately and spent on different things. Clearance answers to deniable work actually completed, not to your rank, so buying grades no longer quietly buys the secrets.
  • Standing orders - Section Three describes how the war is actually going and tells you what to do about it, calibrated against a live measure of how much of the sector's economy the Covenant holds.
  • A fleet operations board - eleven kinds of line work from derelict sweeps to counter-intelligence, opening by service grade rather than clearance, posted against UNSC space and paid in intelligence and influence.
  • Prize crews - win a boarding action with marines aboard and keep the hull, at a price in marines that scales with what you are trying to take.
  • Three desks that do not like each other - Sections One and Two have catalogues of their own now, and buying from one costs you standing with the other two. A desk that owes you charges less; a desk you have ignored for a year charges more, and far enough into the red it declines its best work.
  • Captured technology - Covenant hardware comes off the wrecks you make of them, and three permanent programmes turn it into things the UNSC could never build. The hullmods have no other source: no shop, no cache, no blueprint.
  • A front line that moves - the Covenant gather a suppression force, sail it across the sector under its own power, and burn a world if nobody stops them. Intercept it in transit, break it in orbit, or lose the planet - and killing it costs them months, not a reset.
  • The Great Schism - serve them long enough, and carry enough relics to the vault, and a Sangheili shipmaster asks what you intend to do with what the Oracle actually said. It is the only way out of the Covenant the mod has ever had.
  • Epsilon Eridani, with a graveyard holding the Pillar of Autumn, Iroquois, Gettysburg, In Amber Clad and Forward Unto Dawn - and the Spirit of Fire still drifting, alone, further out. Every one of them still has its flight recorder aboard.
  • Reverence - the stranded battlegroup's anchorage, built around a forge world and covered by its own stations. It is the only Covenant port in the sector, and they are not taking visitors.
  • ONI Section Three on every UNSC world, dealing in fleet stores, ODST detachments, archive access and work nobody writes down.
  • Black operations - six deniable contracts against UNSC hardware in the wrong hands, plus a job board running courier work, dead drops, prisoner transfers, infiltration, extraction and sabotage on the ground with Marines instead of guns. Paid in credits and requisition chits.
  • Requisition and standing - chits buy your way up the twelve-grade UNSC ladder from Warrant Officer to Fleet Admiral, raising your stipend and unlocking what the ONI desk will hand over.
  • Undercover cells in the capital of every other faction in the sector. You will not find one on a menu - at Lieutenant Commander, someone starts waiting for you in the bar, and only after that drink does the door open. They deal in stolen local stores, rewritten records, and whatever nine months of deep cover has quietly put aside.
  • Four custom industries, each taking a colony item only the UNSC makes.
  • Twelve ship systems, six hullmods including a fleet-wide Shipboard AI, and eleven combat missions - two of which put you on the Covenant side of the fight.
  • Custom portraits for both factions, finally, after three versions of borrowed vanilla faces - and the picture picks the name. Choose a UNSC portrait at character creation, and you get a UNSC name; choose a Covenant one, and you very much do not. Their officers and fleet commanders are named the same way.

Compatibility: not save-compatible with the original UNSC mod, and not meant to be run alongside it - both define the same faction and the same ship IDs.

aiDescription: Introduces the UNSC and Covenant as playable factions with ships sized and armed according to canonical lore. Features include a complex ONI clearance system, Covenant devotion mechanics, and a dynamic campaign involving a Forerunner excavation site. The mod also adds the Flood as a hostile faction with unique infested hulls and systems.

changelog.v0.6.2:
Every ship has thirty ordnance points spare. Most of the Covenant line spent its entire budget on the stock loadout, and several UNSC hulls were within a point or two, so the player could not change anything without first taking something off. The room is added to the hull rather than taken out of the loadout - trimming guns would have weakened every ship the AI flies, and the point was to give the player somewhere to put their own ideas. Forty-nine hulls
Eighteen ships were carrying a gun on one flank and a bare mount on the other. The Noryang, the Athens, the Thermopylae, the Sahara, the Thanatos, the Halcyon refit, the Cradle, the Orion, the Sloop and eight Covenant hulls. The missing gun goes into the same weapon group as its opposite number so the pair fires together, and where that pushed a loadout over budget the cost came out of vents
Eighty-seven mounts sat off the edge of the hull. Guns bolted to empty space beside the ship - worst on the Valiant, where two mounts had eleven per cent of their footprint on the hull. Each one is nudged to the nearest position that sits properly on the plating, mirrored pairs moving together so the ship stays symmetrical
Eight spinal guns were mounted crooked, the Paris's MAC most obviously. A gun drawn down the ship's axis with no opposite number belongs at dead centre, and these sat up to eight units to one side
The Infinity could not undock. Sixteen stern point-defence guns were added to a loadout that had two points spare, putting her at 509 of 415. Her armament goes back to what it was; the two stern mounts that sat inside her engine block keep their corrected positions
The Charon's hero variant was over budget too, at 62 of 45, and had been since it was written. It is destroyer-sized and pays destroyer prices for hullmods, which was two thirds of its points. Blast doors and reinforced hull go, the missile racks stay, because three of its nine weapons are Archers
changelog.v0.6.1:
Covenant fighters shoot back. Their guns were declared on the hull instead of on the wing, which is a gun the wing never fires - the same fault the UNSC fighters had before 0.4, never fixed on the other side. Seraphs, Banshees, Phantoms and Spirits have been flying unarmed. Reported by Goblind
Carriers keep launching. Nineteen Covenant hulls carried wings on zero launch bays, so the first sortie went out and nothing replaced it. The engine drops a wing with nowhere to launch from without saying so
Prize crews hand you the ship you boarded. Every captured modded hull was arriving as a Nebula transport. The code asked the engine to build a ship from the captured variant inside a try/catch, on the assumption that an id it cannot resolve throws - it does not, it quietly returns a default hull, so the catch never fired and the fallback was never reached. The id is resolved before use now, and the ship that comes back is checked against the ship that was taken. Reported by DaLintyGuy
Covenant ports sell Covenant weapons. A 0.5 rule aimed at spinal guns drawn into the hull art caught the entire faction, so Reverence stocked nothing while Covenant hulls carried four hundred and fifty-eight fittable slots between them. The seven turret-scale energy weapons are purchasable. The spinal and capital guns stay locked, and no Covenant hull has a free large slot for one anyway. Reported by Goblind
The Independents trade with the Covenant again. A Nexerelin faction config had undone the 0.5.2 fix and put them back to hostile, which starved Covenant markets of everything they do not make themselves. Raised by cvandem
The quiet one at the end of the bar. Buying that drink left the option sitting there and then produced "no rule found for option barLeave" on the way out. A bar scene that ends without offering anything never hands control back to the bar, so the bar never learns the conversation happened. Eight scenes across the ONI cell contact and the surplus yard were ending that way
Guns are the size they are in lore. Every deck gun was drawn at whatever size the sprite happened to be, which is how a single turret ended up a tenth of the length of the ship carrying it. Forty sprites redrawn to scale and every muzzle offset moved to match. The Sabre's autocannon was also borrowing vanilla's art outright and now has its own
Forty-five mounts across twenty-one hulls were inside their own engine blocks, which is where the missile launchers in the Thanatos's exhaust came from. The Tours had all four engines on one flank. The Eion's aft turret was mounted facing sideways. The Constructor's sprite had a two-pixel spike hanging forty rows off her stern, and her collision outline traced it, so she was colliding with - and taking hits on - empty space almost half her own length aft
Two Covenant guns fired the wrong kind of projectile and the Infinity's sixteen stern point-defence mounts were left empty, so the largest ship in the mod had nothing covering her back
Version Checker is wired up - the master file the 0.6 build shipped with still had the placeholder URL in it

releases.modName: Halo - UNSC Reborn - "It Was Locked for a Reason"
Halo - UNSC Reborn - "It Was Locked for a Reason"
releases.changelogNotes:
Devotion is not a substitute for stores. It never has been. It is simply discussed more often.
 The Covenant no longer starve themselves into rebellion. Two markets demanding eleven food between them, producing none, and hostile to every faction in the sector so nothing could be imported. It was permanent by construction, and it ended in unrest on both of their only worlds. This is the whole release.
 The Independents will trade with them. Blanket hostility to everyone is what made the shortage unfixable, because it left no route by which anything could arrive. The Independents are not a power, have no stake in the war, and will sell to anyone holding hard currency - which a fleet that strips worlds has.
 An uncommissioned captain is no longer shot on sight. World generation set the player hostile along with everybody else, so somebody carrying nobody's commission, who had never fired on them, could not dock, could not trade, and could never reach a line of the Ministry dialogue that has been in the mod since 0.5. Take a commission with their enemies, and you are still an enemy, which is the part that was always meant.
 Sanctum had no spaceport. None of any kind, worth roughly -110% accessibility by itself - the market was cut off from shipping entirely, including from the anchorage in its own system.
 Their mines finally feed something. Sanctum produced ore, the anchorage's Orbital Works demanded metals, and no refinery existed anywhere in the faction, so the shipyard had been inert since it was added. There is a refinery now, and it stands at the mines rather than at the shipyard, because ore is heavy.
 Reclamation Vats. A custom industry, because the Covenant do not farm and two of their holdings could not if they wished to. Stripped rock and reclaimed biomass in, protein paste and Unggoy methane out. Nutritionally complete, theologically sanctioned, and every species aboard agrees it is an insult.
 Sacrament Workshops. The other half nobody made: domestic goods and drugs. What a stranded fleet manufactures instead of consumer goods is liturgy - harness and plate for five species that share no anatomy, censers, prayer strips, and the ration narcotics the Ministry issues by rank and declines to call narcotics.
 They can make their own fuel. Fuel Production had demanded volatiles since it was added and nothing in the faction mined any. Sanctum now carries the seam, and the plant sits on top of it rather than a system away
 Reverence has a relay net. Epsilon Eridani has carried a comm relay, a nav buoy and a sensor array since 0.1 and the Covenant carried none of the three, which costs accessibility they could not spare
 The battlegroup has moved five systems further out. They sat close enough to Epsilon Eridani that a starting fleet drifting the obvious direction met a faction hostile to everything that fields nothing under a cruiser. They are not balanced as an early threat and were never meant to be.
 Sanctum is a size 7 forge world rather than a size 5 mining camp, which is what its smelter needed to feed the fleet, and which upgrades its garrison to a High Command.
 Their markets hold a stability floor while trade routes establish. A warfleet under military discipline does not riot about rations.
 An economy audit writes the whole supply and demand picture to the log on every load. It exists because five separate diagnoses of this faction were made by reading industry lists and recalling what vanilla demands, and the measured numbers overturned something every single time - including which market the refinery belonged on, and the fact that the last bottleneck was workforce rather than ore.
